captions.detailed: This 3D model is a hand screwdriver handle designed for 1/4" driver bits. It has a cylindrical, fluted shape with six vertical grip grooves running along its length, creating an ergonomic, easy-to-grip profile. The top of the handle is smoothly rounded, while the bottom section features a narrower, contoured finger grip area. A central hexagonal hole is situated at the bottom for inserting the driver bit, followed by a deeper cylindrical hole intended for a retaining magnet.
captions.instruction: Design a parametric screwdriver handle for standard 1/4" driver bits in OpenSCAD. The handle should feature a hexagonal base body with six vertical flutes for grip, a rounded top end, an ergonomic finger-grip neck near the bottom, and a dual-depth internal hole for the driver bit and a retaining magnet.
captions.factory: The script uses a large cylinder with a low fragment count ($fn=6) as the base handle body. It subtracts a hollowed-out sphere to round off the top end, and uses a larger cylinder difference to round the outer corners. Six vertical cylinders are subtracted in a loop to create the flutes. The ergonomic neck is carved out using two scaled circles swept via rotate_extrude. Finally, a hexagonal cylinder ($fn=6) is subtracted for the bit hole, and a deeper cylindrical shaft is subtracted for the magnet.
